title: Panelo links threats to VP’s ex-staff to government
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp believes that the alleged threats made against a former member of her household staff could be linked to the Marcos administration.

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp believes that the alleged threats made against a former member of her household staff could be linked to the Marcos administration.
Duterte spokesman Paolo Panelo issued a statement yesterday and disclosed that at 11:19 p.m. on Monday, the Vice President received a text message from her former staff.

“The message contained a desperate plea for help and rescue in Manila. The sender claimed to be in the custody or under the control of certain individuals who allegedly told them about a threat to their lives,” he said.
The message sender alleged that they were being forced to sign a document but they refused.

“We are deeply concerned that this incident may be part of what we believe to be a relentless campaign by the Marcos administration, utilizing state institutions like the NBI (National Bureau of Investigation), against the Vice President,” Panelo added.
He mentioned similarities with the incident concerning Jefry Tupas, the former chief information officer of Davao City when the Vice President was still city mayor.
On Sept. 29, NBI agents allegedly told Tupas that there were threats to his life and attempted to bring him to Manila.
Panelo said at the time he wrote the statement, they had no idea of the whereabouts of the former household staff, and have yet to independently verify the staff’s safety and well-being.

He explained that they brought the incident to the public and media’s attention because of the alleged “unremitting efforts of the government to harass, threaten and coerce individuals into becoming false witnesses in support of trumped-up charges against VP Sara Duterte, weaponize state agencies and undermine the rule of law for political ends.”
“The safety and liberty of this former staff member must be guaranteed without delay,” Panelo added.
Palace: Fake news
Asked to react to Panelo’s statement, Palace press officer Claire Castro said the Marcos administration is not in the business of sowing intrigue and fabricating evidence.

“Creating intrigue and planting evidence are not being done at present, things that the Duterte administration was used to doing and this was admitted by former president Duterte before the media,” she said.
“There is no room for fake news under the present administration,” said Castro.
However, Castro said the claim should be investigated to determine if it is true.
PNP: File report
The Philippine National Police urged the Vice President’s camp to come forward with the information that her former household staff is being held against their will by a group of people.
PNP spokesman Brig. Gen. Allen Rae Co said Duterte or any representative has yet to file a formal report to the police.
“The trigger that will start our investigation is if they will formally or at least personally report it to us, not through social media,” he said at a news briefing.
Co assured Duterte they are ready to assist in efforts to locate her former household staff, stressing the PNP is always ready to protect anyone regardless of political affiliations.
The NBI also urged Duterte to file a formal report, saying it cannot investigate claims circulating only on social media.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said yesterday the bureau had received no formal complaint or referral regarding the reported incident, despite what he described as coordinated social media posts about the alleged disappearance of the Vice President’s former staff members. — Alexis Romero, Emmanuel Tupas, Mark Ernest Villeza
